title: CRLR/757/2022 of MAHAVIR SINGH RAWAT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH ITS SECRETARY HOME, CIVIL SECRETARIAT DEHRADUN U.K.

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 757 of 2022
With
Compounding Application IA No. 1 of 2022
Mahavir Singh Rawat and Others ...Revisionists
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and Another ...Respondents
Present:-
Ms. Abhilasha Belwal, Advocate for the revisionists.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Pawan Mishra, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Ashish
Belwal, Advocate for the respondent no.2.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The revisionist seeks quashing of chargesheet dated
09.04.2015, cognizance order dated 06.08.2015, passed in
Criminal Case No.2674 of 2015, State Vs. Mahavir Singh
Rawat and Others, under Sections 498-A, 323, 504 and 506
IPC and Section 3⁄4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, by the
court of II Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, District
Dehradun ("the case") as well as the entire proceedings of the
case on the basis of amicable settlement between the parties.
2. The revisionists and the respondent no.2 ("the
informant") have filed a joint Compounding Application No. 1 of
2022 alongwith the affidavits.
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.

2
4. Learned counsel for the parties would submit that
parties had earlier filed C-482 No. 2178 of 2022 for seeking
relief as sought in this petition, but that that was withdrawn in
view of the observation by the Court that a revision is
maintainable in the case.
5. It is also submitted on behalf of the revisionists that
parties have amicably settled the dispute and the informant
has decided to stay separate.
6. Today, the revisionist no.1, Mr. Mahavir Singh
Rawat, and the informant, Anita Gusain, both have joined the
proceedings of the Court in person, as identified by their
respective counsel.
7. Both the parties have accepted the compromise. The
Court particularly asked the informant about the settlement.
She would submit that the matter has been settled between the
parties.
8. Since this is a matrimonial discord and the
parties have amicably settled the dispute, this Court is of the
view that it is a case, which may be decided on the basis of
amicable settlement between the parties. Accordingly, the
revision deserves to be allowed.

3
9. The charge sheet dated 09.04.2015,
summoning order dated 06.08.2015 as well as the entire
proceedings of the case are hereby quashed.
10. Compounding Application No. 1 of 2022 stands
disposed of, accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 22.12.2022
Ravi Bisht
